 Rabada gives Proteas strong start at Wanderers
 Kagiso Rabada claimed three wickets before Tanzid Hasan’s unbeaten half-century helped Bangladesh recover on the opening morning of the first Test at the Wanderers on Sunday.
 The tourists reached lunch on 91-3 after 26 overs, having slumped to 22-3 following their decision to bat.
 Tanzid was unbeaten on 51 from 82 deliveries, including nine fours, with Towhid Hridoy on 23. Their unbroken fourth-wicket partnership of 69 gave Bangladesh a foothold after Rabada threatened to tear through the batting order.
 Watch: Rabada wastes no time 
 The Proteas spearhead struck with the first ball of the match, finding Mahfijul Islam’s outside edge for Marco Jansen to take the catch at fourth slip.
 Mominul Haque also departed without scoring, edging Rabada behind to wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton in the third over to leave Bangladesh 2-2.
 Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto struck two boundaries in his 12, sharing a brief partnership of 20 with Tanzid before Rabada produced the morning’s standout delivery.
 The ball jagged back through the gap between bat and pad to hit off stump, giving the fast bowler his third wicket inside nine overs.
 KG Rabada picks it out of the ground 🤩💥
 That’s three for South Africa in the session 🇿🇦🏏

 Tanzid and Hridoy then settled into their partnership, surviving the early pressure before finding more opportunities to score.
 Tanzid was particularly positive, punishing width and advancing down the pitch to loft Dane Paterson for four during the latter stages of the session.
 The pair added 45 runs in the final 10 overs before lunch, taking Bangladesh towards three figures and giving the Proteas a fresh challenge after their excellent start.
